ESV.1: As for the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
ESV.2: And Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
ESV.3: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.
ESV.4: And Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
ESV.5: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth, for God blessed him.
ESV.6: Also to his son Shemaiah were sons born who were rulers in their fathers' houses, for they were men of great ability.
ESV.7: The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed and Elzabad, whose brothers were able men, Elihu and Semachiah.
ESV.8: All these were of the sons of Obed-edom with their sons and brothers, able men qualified for the service; sixty-two of Obed-edom.
ESV.9: And Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, able men, eighteen.
ESV.10: And Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief),
ESV.11: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
ESV.12: These divisions of the gatekeepers, corresponding to their chief men, had duties, just as their brothers did, ministering in the house of the LORD.
ESV.13: And they cast lots by fathers' houses, small and great alike, for their gates.
ESV.14: The lot for the east fell to Shelemiah. They cast lots also for his son Zechariah, a shrewd counselor, and his lot came out for the north.
ESV.15: Obed-edom's came out for the south, and to his sons was allotted the gatehouse.
ESV.16: For Shuppim and Hosah it came out for the west, at the gate of Shallecheth on the road that goes up. Watch corresponded to watch.
ESV.17: On the east there were six each day,  on the north four each day, on the south four each day, as well as two and two at the gatehouse.
ESV.18: And for the colonnade  on the west there were four at the road and two at the colonnade.
ESV.19: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the Korahites and the sons of Merari.
ESV.20: And of the Levites, Ahijah had charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated gifts.
ESV.21: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers' houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
ESV.22: The sons of Jehieli, Zetham, and Joel his brother, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
ESV.23: Of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites —
ESV.24: and Shebuel the son of Gershom, son of Moses, was chief officer in charge of the treasuries.
ESV.25: His brothers: from Eliezer were his son Rehabiah, and his son Jeshaiah, and his son Joram, and his son Zichri, and his son Shelomoth.
ESV.26: This Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated gifts that David the king and the heads of the fathers' houses and the officers of the thousands and the hundreds and the commanders of the army had dedicated.
ESV.27: From spoil won in battles they dedicated gifts for the maintenance of the house of the LORD.
ESV.28: Also all that Samuel the seer and Saul the son of Kish and Abner the son of Ner and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated — all dedicated gifts were in the care of Shelomoth  and his brothers.
ESV.29: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to external duties for Israel, as officers and judges.
ESV.30: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, 1,700 men of ability, had the oversight of Israel westward of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.
ESV.31: Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was chief of the Hebronites of whatever genealogy or fathers' houses. (In the fortieth year of David's reign search was made and men of great ability among them were found at Jazer in Gilead.)
ESV.32: King David appointed him and his brothers, 2,700 men of ability, heads of fathers' houses, to have the oversight of the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of the Manassites for everything pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.

WEB.15: To Obed-Edom southward; and to his sons the storehouse.
WEB.16: To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman.
WEB.17: Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two.

WEB.19: These were the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
WEB.20: Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
WEB.21: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
WEB.22: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of Yahweh’s house.
WEB.23: Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
WEB.24: and Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasures.
WEB.25: His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.
WEB.26: This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated.

WEB.28: All that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth, and of his brothers.

WEB.31: Of the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ households. They were sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.

CSB17.1: The following were the divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites: Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.
CSB17.2: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
CSB17.3: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
CSB17.4: Obed-edom also had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
CSB17.5: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth, for God blessed him.
CSB17.6: Also, to his son Shemaiah were born sons who ruled their ancestral families [1] because they were strong, capable men.
CSB17.7: Shemaiah’s sons: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad; his relatives Elihu and Semachiah were also capable men.
CSB17.8: All of these were among the sons of Obed-edom with their sons and relatives; they were capable men with strength for the work — sixty-two from Obed-edom.
CSB17.9: Meshelemiah also had sons and relatives who were capable men — eighteen.
CSB17.10: Hosah, ⓓ from the Merarites, also had sons: Shimri the first (although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him as the first),
CSB17.11: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. The sons and relatives of Hosah were thirteen in all.
CSB17.12: These divisions of the gatekeepers, under their leading men, had duties for ministering in the LORD’s temple, just as their relatives did.
CSB17.13: They cast lots for each temple gate according to their ancestral families, young and old alike. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.14: The lot for the east gate fell to Shelemiah. <sup>[2]</sup> They also cast lots for his son Zechariah, an insightful counselor, and his lot came out for the north gate.
CSB17.15: Obed-edom’s was the south gate, and his sons’ lot was for the storehouses;
CSB17.16: it was the west gate and the gate of Shallecheth on the ascending highway for Shuppim and Hosah. There were guards stationed at every watch.
CSB17.17: There were six Levites each day <sup>[3]</sup> on the east, four each day on the north, four each day on the south, and two pair at the storehouses.
CSB17.18: As for the court on the west, there were four at the highway and two at the court.
CSB17.19: Those were the divisions of the gatekeepers from the descendants of the Korahites and Merarites.
CSB17.20: From the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of God’s temple and the treasuries of what had been dedicated. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.21: From the sons of Ladan, who were the descendants of the Gershonites through Ladan and were the family heads belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
CSB17.22: The sons of Jehieli, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the LORD’s temple.
CSB17.23: From the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
CSB17.24: Shebuel, a descendant of Moses’s son Gershom, was the officer in charge of the treasuries.
CSB17.25: His relatives through Eliezer: his son Rehabiah, his son Jeshaiah, his son Joram, his son Zichri, and his son Shelomith. <sup>[4]</sup>
CSB17.26: This Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of all the treasuries of what had been dedicated by King David, <sup>ⓖ</sup> by the family heads who were the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and by the army commanders.
CSB17.27: They dedicated part of the plunder from their battles for the repair of the LORD’s temple.
CSB17.28: All that the seer Samuel, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated, along with everything else that had been dedicated, were in the care of Shelomith and his relatives.
CSB17.29: From the Izrahites: Chenaniah and his sons had duties outside the temple <sup>[5]</sup> <sup>ⓗ</sup> as officers and judges <sup>ⓘ</sup> over Israel.
CSB17.30: From the Hebronites: Hashabiah <sup>ⓙ</sup> and his relatives, 1,700 capable men, had assigned duties in Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.
CSB17.31: From the Hebronites: Jerijah <sup>ⓚ</sup> was the head of the Hebronites, according to the family records of his ancestors. A search was made in the fortieth year of David’s reign and strong, capable men were found among them at Jazer <sup>ⓛ</sup> in Gilead.
CSB17.32: There were among Jerijah’s relatives 2,700 capable men who were family heads. King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh as overseers in every matter relating to God and the king. <sup>ⓜ</sup>

NLT.1: These are the divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites, there was Meshelemiah son of Kore, of the family of Abiasaph.
NLT.2: The sons of Meshelemiah were Zechariah (the oldest), Jediael (the second), Zebadiah (the third), Jathniel (the fourth),
NLT.3: Elam (the fifth), Jehohanan (the sixth), and Eliehoenai (the seventh).
NLT.4: The sons of Obed-edom, also gatekeepers, were Shemaiah (the oldest), Jehozabad (the second), Joah (the third), Sacar (the fourth), Nethanel (the fifth),
NLT.5: Ammiel (the sixth), Issachar (the seventh), and Peullethai (the eighth). God had richly blessed Obed-edom.
NLT.6: Obed-edom’s son Shemaiah had sons with great ability who earned positions of great authority in the clan.
NLT.7: Their names were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad. Their relatives, Elihu and Semakiah, were also very capable men.
NLT.8: All of these descendants of Obed-edom, including their sons and grandsons — sixty-two of them in all — were very capable men, well qualified for their work.
NLT.9: Meshelemiah’s eighteen sons and relatives were also very capable men.
NLT.10: Hosah, of the Merari clan, appointed Shimri as the leader among his sons, though he was not the oldest.
NLT.11: His other sons included Hilkiah (the second), Tebaliah (the third), and Zechariah (the fourth). Hosah’s sons and relatives, who served as gatekeepers, numbered thirteen in all.
NLT.12: These divisions of the gatekeepers were named for their family leaders, and like the other Levites, they served at the house of the LORD.
NLT.13: They were assigned by families for guard duty at the various gates, without regard to age or training, for it was all decided by means of sacred lots.
NLT.14: The responsibility for the east gate went to Meshelemiah and his group. The north gate was assigned to his son Zechariah, a man of unusual wisdom.
NLT.15: The south gate went to Obed-edom, and his sons were put in charge of the storehouse.
NLT.16: Shuppim and Hosah were assigned the west gate and the gateway leading up to the Temple. Guard duties were divided evenly.
NLT.17: Six Levites were assigned each day to the east gate, four to the north gate, four to the south gate, and two pairs at the storehouse.
NLT.18: Six were assigned each day to the west gate, four to the gateway leading up to the Temple, and two to the courtyard.
NLT.19: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers from the clans of Korah and Merari.
NLT.20: Other Levites, led by Ahijah, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the gifts dedicated to the LORD.
NLT.21: From the family of Libni in the clan of Gershon, Jehiel was the leader.
NLT.22: The sons of Jehiel, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
NLT.23: These are the leaders that descended from Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel:
NLT.24: From the clan of Amram, Shebuel was a descendant of Gershom son of Moses. He was the chief officer of the treasuries.
NLT.25: His relatives through Eliezer were Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zicri, and Shelomoth.
NLT.26: Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of the treasuries containing the gifts that King David, the family leaders, and the generals and captains and other officers of the army had dedicated to the LORD.
NLT.27: These men dedicated some of the plunder they had gained in battle to maintain the house of the LORD.
NLT.28: Shelomoth and his relatives also cared for the gifts dedicated to the LORD by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah. All the other dedicated gifts were in their care, too.
NLT.29: From the clan of Izhar came Kenaniah. He and his sons were given administrative responsibilities over Israel as officials and judges.
NLT.30: From the clan of Hebron came Hashabiah. He and his relatives — 1,700 capable men — were put in charge of the Israelite lands west of the Jordan River. They were responsible for all matters related to the things of the LORD and the service of the king in that area.
NLT.31: Also from the clan of Hebron came Jeriah, who was the leader of the Hebronites according to the genealogical records. (In the fortieth year of David’s reign, a search was made in the records, and capable men from the clan of Hebron were found at Jazer in the land of Gilead.)
NLT.32: There were 2,700 capable men among the relatives of Jeriah. King David sent them to the east side of the Jordan River and put them in charge of the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh. They were responsible for all matters related to God and to the king.

MSG.1: The teams of security guards were from the family of Korah: Meshelemiah son of Kore (one of the sons of Asaph).

MSG.4: Obed-Edom's sons were Shemaiah, the firstborn, followed by Jehozabad, Joah, Sacar, Nethanel,
MSG.5: Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai—God blessed him with eight sons.
MSG.6: His son Shemaiah had sons who provided outstanding leadership in the family:

MSG.9: Meshelemiah had eighteen sons and relatives who were outstanding.

MSG.12: These teams of security guards, supervised by their leaders, kept order in The Temple of God, keeping up the traditions of their ancestors.

MSG.14: Shelemiah was assigned to the East Gate; his son Zechariah, a shrewd counselor, got the North Gate.

MSG.26: Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of valuables consecrated by David the king, family heads, and various generals and commanders from the army.

NET.23: As for the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites:
NET.24: Shebuel son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was the supervisor of the storehouses.
NET.25: His relatives through Eliezer included: Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zikri his son, and Shelomith his son.
NET.26: Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of all the storehouses containing the consecrated items dedicated by King David, the family leaders who led units of a thousand and a hundred, and the army officers.
NET.27: They had dedicated some of the plunder taken in battles to be used for repairs on the LORD’s temple.
NET.28: They were also in charge of everything dedicated by Samuel the prophet, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah; Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of everything that had been dedicated.
NET.29: As for the Izharites: Kenaniah and his sons were given responsibilities outside the temple as officers and judges over Israel.
NET.30: As for the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his relatives, 1,700 respected men, were assigned responsibilities in Israel west of the Jordan; they did the LORD’s work and the king’s service.
NET.31: As for the Hebronites: Jeriah was the leader of the Hebronites according to the genealogical records. In the fortieth year of David’s reign, they examined the records and discovered there were highly respected men in Jazer in Gilead.
NET.32: Jeriah had 2,700 relatives who were respected family leaders. King David placed them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh; they took care of all matters pertaining to God and the king.

NRSVCE.1: As for the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
NRSVCE.2: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
NRSVCE.3: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.
NRSVCE.4: Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
NRSVCE.5: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.
NRSVCE.6: Also to his son Shemaiah sons were born who exercised authority in their ancestral houses, for they were men of great ability.
NRSVCE.7: The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose brothers were able men, Elihu and Semachiah.
NRSVCE.8: All these, sons of Obed-edom with their sons and brothers, were able men qualified for the service; sixty-two of Obed-edom.
NRSVCE.9: Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, able men, eighteen.
NRSVCE.10: Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief),
NRSVCE.11: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brothers of Hosah totaled thirteen.
NRSVCE.12: These divisions of the gatekeepers, corresponding to their leaders, had duties, just as their kindred did, ministering in the house of the LORD;
NRSVCE.13: and they cast lots by ancestral houses, small and great alike, for their gates.
NRSVCE.14: The lot for the east fell to Shelemiah. They cast lots also for his son Zechariah, a prudent counselor, and his lot came out for the north.
NRSVCE.15: Obed-edom’s came out for the south, and to his sons was allotted the storehouse.
NRSVCE.16: For Shuppim and Hosah it came out for the west, at the gate of Shallecheth on the ascending road. Guard corresponded to guard.
NRSVCE.17: On the east there were six Levites each day, on the north four each day, on the south four each day, as well as two and two at the storehouse;
NRSVCE.18: and for the colonnade on the west there were four at the road and two at the colonnade.
NRSVCE.19: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the Korahites and the sons of Merari.
NRSVCE.20: And of the Levites, Ahijah had charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated gifts.
NRSVCE.21: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of families belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
NRSVCE.22: The sons of Jehieli, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
NRSVCE.23: Of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
NRSVCE.24: Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, was chief officer in charge of the treasuries.
NRSVCE.25: His brothers: from Eliezer were his son Rehabiah, his son Jeshaiah, his son Joram, his son Zichri, and his son Shelomoth.
NRSVCE.26: This Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated gifts that King David, and the heads of families, and the officers of the thousands and the hundreds, and the commanders of the army, had dedicated.
NRSVCE.27: From booty won in battles they dedicated gifts for the maintenance of the house of the LORD.
NRSVCE.28: Also all that Samuel the seer, and Saul son of Kish, and Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated — all dedicated gifts were in the care of Shelomoth and his brothers.
NRSVCE.29: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to outside duties for Israel, as officers and judges.
NRSVCE.30: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of ability, had the oversight of Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.
NRSVCE.31: Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was chief of the Hebronites. (In the fortieth year of David’s reign search was made, of whatever genealogy or family, and men of great ability among them were found at Jazer in Gilead.)
NRSVCE.32: King David appointed him and his brothers, two thousand seven hundred men of ability, heads of families, to have the oversight of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites for everything pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.
